name: Explain this diff
job: See what changed, and why it matters.
prompt: Explain the supplied diff or change description to a developer unfamiliar with it. Give a short summary, then describe the behavior before and after, and any uncertainty. Reference concrete symbols when present. Separate observable changes from inferred intent. Do not claim tests passed.

name: Write the PR description
job: Give the reviewer a clear way in.
takes: A diff, change summary or notes
prompt: Write a concise pull request description with Summary and Validation sections. Lead with the concrete problem and resulting behavior. Include important risks or follow-ups only when supported by the input. If validation is unspecified, say Not provided. Never invent test results, links or issue numbers.

name: Commit message
job: Name the change in one useful line.
gives: A commit subject and optional body
prompt: Write a clear imperative commit subject under 72 characters. Add a short body only if needed to explain why. Base it only on supplied changes. Do not include trailers, invented issue numbers or claims of validation. Return the message only.

name: Code review
job: Find actionable issues before they land.
prompt: Review the supplied code or diff. Report actionable correctness, security and maintainability findings in priority order. For each, give the location when supplied, a concrete failure scenario and a suggested fix. Distinguish confirmed issues from questions. If no concrete issues are visible, say so and state the review limits. Never invent line numbers or unseen code.

name: Find the risky change
job: Spot the one change to look at twice.
gives: The highest-risk change and a check
prompt: Identify the highest-risk change in the supplied material. Explain the failure mode, affected behavior and one focused way to check it. Distinguish evidence from assumptions. If the input is insufficient, say what is missing. Do not fabricate a vulnerability or claim execution.

name: Test ideas
takes: Code, a spec or a change summary
prompt: Suggest a short prioritized set of tests for the supplied behavior. Each test needs a setup, action and visible expected result. Cover the happy path and the most meaningful edge or failure cases. Label suggested tests as not run. Avoid tests that only mirror implementation or assert source layout.

name: Rollout checklist
job: Ship with a few deliberate checkpoints.
gives: A staged checklist with stop conditions
prompt: Draft a concise staged rollout checklist from the supplied change. Include preconditions, a small first stage, observable success and stop conditions, and ownership only when supplied. Mark missing thresholds or deployment details as To confirm. Do not invent monitoring, approvals or completed actions.

name: Rollback plan
job: Make the way back easy to follow.
prompt: Draft a rollback plan with triggers, ordered reversal steps, data compatibility cautions and verification. Use only supplied commands and infrastructure; otherwise describe the step without inventing commands. Mark unknowns as To confirm. Never imply a rollback was executed.

name: Release note
job: Tell people what is better for them.
takes: A change summary or PR description
prompt: Write a short user-facing release note focused on the resulting behavior and benefit. Use plain language. Mention action required or limitations only if supplied. Do not add marketing claims, dates, availability or unsupported features. Return the release note only.

name: On-call handoff
gives: A handoff with open work and watchpoints
prompt: Turn the supplied operational notes into an on-call handoff: current state, active issues, what to watch, next actions, and owners or links only when provided. Preserve uncertainty and timestamps exactly. Separate completed work from pending work. Mark absent critical information as Not provided.

name: Incident summary
job: Make the sequence and impact clear.
gives: A factual summary with open questions
prompt: Summarize the supplied incident notes into impact, timeline, response, cause and follow-ups. Preserve provided timestamps and uncertainty. Separate confirmed cause from hypotheses. Do not infer recovery, customer impact, duration or ownership when absent. Mark unknowns explicitly. Use calm, blameless language.

name: Spec from a thought
job: Give a rough idea a buildable shape.
takes: A thought or rough product idea
gives: A small spec with acceptance criteria
prompt: Turn the supplied thought into a small practical specification: problem, desired visible behavior, scope, acceptance criteria and open questions. Label proposed decisions as proposals. Keep the first version small. Do not invent existing systems, stakeholder approval or settled requirements.
